calls.reason: The blog keeps humans setting direction, but it also describes agents proposing hypotheses and designing every experiment on an open research problem. That is more than 'just faster coding'.

No source separates harness and tool gains from model gains for the blog's results. Anthropic's managed-agents post says a newer model made one harness fix unnecessary, which cuts against crediting harnesses alone.
A 2022 Northeastern report confirms he argued for hybrid models. Nothing in the packet shows neurosymbolic supplementation was necessary, and a newer model removing a harness fix cuts the other way.
The only evidence is a May 2026 paper on how to measure progress toward AGI. Nothing assesses the leading systems' broad, autonomous capability as of June 2026.
The blog's results are coding and research benchmarks plus internal data on speeding up AI development, framed as a possible path to RSI. It shows nothing like broad human-level autonomy.
The blog itself says it is 'not there yet' on RSI and that humans still chose the problems. The research-agent work goes beyond a coding tool, but the main point that RSI was not shown holds.
